## 8.1 Rules and Bets

Blackjack (also called 21) is played with a standard 52-card deck. Players try to reach a hand total closer to 21 than the dealer's without exceeding it. Card values:

- Numbered cards: face value
- Jack, Queen, King: 10 points each
- Ace: 1 or 11 points (whichever is more advantageous)

The dealer plays a fixed strategy: hit until the hand totals 17 or more, then stay. Each player resolves their hand before the dealer plays. Key player options are **hit**, **stay**, **double-down**, **split**, **surrender**, and **insurance**.

## 8.2 Basic Strategy in Blackjack

Because the dealer plays a fixed strategy and shows one card face-up, the player can adapt accordingly. Additionally, cards are dealt without replacement from a shared deck, so outcomes across rounds are *dependent* — unlike roulette or craps.

### Dealer hand probabilities (multiple decks)

The following simulation estimates the probability of each possible dealer outcome assuming sampling with replacement (approximating a large number of decks).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-8_1code

set.seed(8675)
n          <- 100000
cardvalues <- rep(c(seq(1, 10), rep(10, 3)), each = 4)   # J/Q/K = 10; Ace = 1
outcome    <- rep(0, n)

for (i in 1:n) {
  hand <- sample(cardvalues, 2, replace = TRUE)
  sw   <- TRUE

  while (sw) {
    isace <- (hand == 1)

    if (sum(isace) > 0) {
      # Use Ace as 11 if it doesn't bust, otherwise as 1
      if (sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace) + 10 > 21) {
        handvalue <- sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace)
      } else {
        handvalue <- sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace) + 10
      }
    } else {
      handvalue <- sum(hand)
    }

    if (handvalue >= 17) {
      sw <- FALSE
    } else {
      hand <- c(hand, sample(cardvalues, 1))
    }
  }

  if (handvalue > 21) {
    outcome[i] <- "Bust"
  } else if (handvalue == 21 & length(hand) == 2) {
    outcome[i] <- "Blackjack!"
  } else {
    outcome[i] <- handvalue
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-8_1
#| tbl-cap: "Dealer hand probabilities"

outcomes <- outcome %>%
    table() %>%
    proportions() %>%
    round(3) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    setNames(c("Outcome", "Probability")) %>%
    mutate(Probability = scales::percent(Probability, accuracy = 0.1))

outcomes %>%
    flextable() 
```

Key takeaways from table 8.1:

- The dealer busts roughly **28% of the time** — about once every four rounds
- A hand of 20 is the most common non-bust outcome (~18%)
- This suggests a defensive player strategy can be profitable when the dealer is likely to bust

### Conditional probabilities by face-up card

The simulation above ignores the information available from the dealer's face-up card. We can simulate hand probabilities conditional on the dealer's card facing up. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-8_2code
#| cache: true

set.seed(5512)
n          <- 50000
cardvalues <- rep(c(seq(1, 10), rep(10, 3)), each = 4)

sim_conditional <- function(face_up, n, cardvalues) {
  outcomes <- character(n)
  for (i in 1:n) {
    hole <- sample(cardvalues, 1)
    hand <- c(face_up, hole)
    if ((face_up == 1 & hole == 10) | (face_up == 10 & hole == 1)) {
      outcomes[i] <- "BJ"; next
    }
    sw <- TRUE
    while (sw) {
      isace <- (hand == 1)
      if (sum(isace) > 0) {
        handvalue <- if (sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace) + 10 > 21)
          sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace) else sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace) + 10
      } else {
        handvalue <- sum(hand)
      }
      if (handvalue >= 17) sw <- FALSE
      else hand <- c(hand, sample(cardvalues, 1))
    }
    outcomes[i] <- if (handvalue > 21) "Bust" else as.character(handvalue)
  }
  outcomes
}

lvls <- c("17", "18", "19", "20", "21", "BJ", "Bust")

ot <- mapply(\(fv, lab) {
  out <- sim_conditional(fv, n, cardvalues)
  c(`Face-up` = lab, round(table(factor(out, levels = lvls)) / n, 3))
}, c(1, 2:9, 10), c("A", as.character(2:9), "10/J/Q/K"),
SIMPLIFY = FALSE) |>
  do.call(rbind, args = _) |>
  as.data.frame() 


```

```{r}
#| label:   Table-8_2
#| tbl-cap: "Dealer hand probabilities conditional on face-up card"

outcomes8.2 <- ot %>%
    as.data.frame()

outcomes8.2 %>%
    flextable()
```

The bust probability is substantially higher when the face-up card is 4, 5, or 6, and lower when it is 7 or above. This motivates the **basic strategy**:

| Dealer's face-up card | Player's recommended action |
|---|---|
| 4, 5, or 6 | Stay with 12 or more (very defensive) |
| 2 or 3 | Stay with 13 or more |
| 7 or higher (or Ace) | Stay with 17 or more; hit otherwise |

The rationale: when the dealer shows a low card, the most likely scenario is the dealer drawing to a stiff hand (12–16) and then busting on the next card. Playing defensively avoids the player also busting.

## 8.3 A Gambling System That Works: Card Counting

A critical feature of blackjack is that cards are **not reshuffled between rounds**. The composition of the remaining deck changes throughout a shoe, which can shift probabilities substantially.

### Effect of a depleted deck

To illustrate, consider a single deck from which all Aces and 2–6s have been removed, leaving only 28 cards (7s, 8s, 9s, and 10-valued cards). Since there are no low cards to rescue a stiff hand, the dealer's outcome distribution changes dramatically.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-8_4-code
set.seed(3091)
n          <- 100000
cardvalues <- rep(c(seq(7, 10), rep(10, 3)), each = 4)   # 28 cards remaining
tab8.4    <- rep(0, n)

for (i in 1:n) {
  shuffleddeck <- sample(cardvalues, length(cardvalues), replace = FALSE)
  hand         <- shuffleddeck[1:2]
  currentcard  <- 3
  sw           <- TRUE

  while (sw) {
    isace <- (hand == 1)   # no Aces in depleted deck; retained for generality

    if (sum(isace) > 0) {
      if (sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace) + 10 > 21) {
        handvalue <- sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace)
      } else {
        handvalue <- sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace) + 10
      }
    } else {
      handvalue <- sum(hand)
    }

    if (handvalue >= 17) {
      sw <- FALSE
    } else {
      hand        <- c(hand, shuffleddeck[currentcard])
      currentcard <- currentcard + 1
    }
  }

  if (handvalue > 21) {
    tab8.4[i] <- "Bust"
  } else if (handvalue == 21 & length(hand) == 2) {
    tab8.4[i] <- "BJ"
  } else {
    tab8.4[i] <- handvalue
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-8_4
#| tbl-cap: "Hand probability, single deck, dealer stays, Aces, 2s–6s removed"

outcomes8.4 <- tab8.4 %>%
    table() %>%
    proportions() %>%
    round(3) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    setNames(c("Outcome", "Probability")) %>%
    mutate(Probability = scales::percent(Probability, accuracy = 0.1))

outcomes8.4 %>%
    flextable() 
```

This reproduces **Table 8.4**. Comparing against the full-deck simulation:

| Outcome | Full deck (Table 8.1) | Depleted deck (Table 8.4) |
|---|---|---|
| 17 | 0.145 | 0.212 |
| 18 | 0.140 | 0.186 |
| 19 | 0.134 | 0.170 |
| 20 | 0.180 | 0.317 |
| 21 | 0.073 | 0.001 |
| BJ | 0.047 | 0.000 |
| Bust | 0.282 | 0.115 |

With all low cards gone: bust rate falls from 28% to 12%, and 20 becomes the dominant outcome (32%). The player's optimal strategy shifts accordingly.

### The Hi-Lo card counting system

Card counting exploits the changing deck composition by tracking which cards have been played. The simplest system in practice is the **Hi-Lo count**:

| Cards | Count adjustment |
|---|---|
| 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 | +1 |
| 7, 8, 9 | 0 |
| 10, J, Q, K, A | −1 |

A high count signals many high cards remaining, which benefits the player (higher probability of dealer busting, higher probability of natural blackjack at 3:2 payout). One threshold strategy for single-deck games:

| Count | Bet multiplier |
|---|---|
| ≤ +1 | 1× (table minimum) |
| +2 to +3 | 2× |
| +4 to +5 | 3× |
| +6 to +7 | 4× |
| +8 or more | 5× |

## 8.4 Exercises

Selected R exercises from the chapter:

**Exercise 13** — Modify the Section 8.2 simulation to use a single deck with sampling *without* replacement:

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Exercise 13 solution"
set.seed(2241)
n          <- 100000
cardvalues <- rep(c(seq(1, 10), rep(10, 3)), each = 4)
outcome    <- rep(0, n)

for (i in 1:n) {
  shuffleddeck <- sample(cardvalues, length(cardvalues), replace = FALSE)
  hand         <- shuffleddeck[1:2]
  currentcard  <- 3
  sw           <- TRUE

  while (sw) {
    isace <- (hand == 1)
    if (sum(isace) > 0) {
      if (sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace) + 10 > 21) {
        handvalue <- sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace)
      } else {
        handvalue <- sum(hand[!isace]) + sum(isace) + 10
      }
    } else {
      handvalue <- sum(hand)
    }
    if (handvalue >= 17) {
      sw <- FALSE
    } else {
      hand        <- c(hand, shuffleddeck[currentcard])
      currentcard <- currentcard + 1
    }
  }

  if (handvalue > 21) {
    outcome[i] <- "Bust"
  } else if (handvalue == 21 & length(hand) == 2) {
    outcome[i] <- "BJ"
  } else {
    outcome[i] <- handvalue
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-8_5
#| tbl-cap: "Hand probability, single deck, dealer stays, Aces, 2s–6s removed"

outcomes8.4 <- tab8.4 %>%
    table() %>%
    proportions() %>%
    round(3) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    setNames(c("Outcome", "Probability")) %>%
    mutate(Probability = scales::percent(Probability, accuracy = 0.1))

outcomes8.4 %>%
    flextable() 
```

The single-deck results differ slightly from Table 8.1 because removing each card meaningfully changes the remaining composition.
